sentences.text: This creature measured about four meters across its wings.
Its head featured a long, sharp beak with slender, cone-shaped teeth at the jaw tips.
While other Brazilian flying reptiles often bore head crests, this one did not show them on its snout or chin.
Recent research from 2026 indicates a different jaw specimen actually supports the presence of a chin ridge.
Fossils were unearthed in the lower Santana Formation within the Chapada do Araripe region of Ceará, Brazil.
Alexander Wilhelm Armin Kellner first gave this animal its name in 1984.
The defining specimen, cataloged as MN 4804-V, preserves only the front section of a lower jaw.
Scientists place this animal within the broader group known as Ornithocheiroidea.
It belongs to the class Reptilia.

Taxonomic opinions have shifted over time; Kellner moved it from Ornithocheiridae to uncertain Pterodactyloidea, then suggested a link to Anhangueridae, while others proposed connections to Anhanguera, Coloborhynchus, or even treated Ludodactylus as a synonym.
This reptile lived during the Aptian stage, roughly between 119.57 and 113.2 million years ago.
